newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China, Britain strike deal on HK's 1997/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: China, Britain strike deal on HK's 1997/98 budget.

text.p: Britain and China on Tuesday approved Hong Kong's budget, eight days before Financial Secretary Donald Tsang unveils spending plans for the territory which will straddle the handover to China.
"I'm glad to say that after 19 rounds of talks ... we have now successfully finished preparations for the 1997/98 budget," said Kwong Ki-chi, Hong Kong's Secretary for the Treasury.
Kwong sat as a representative of the British team in the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG) talks on the transitional budget which have dragged on for about two years.
The JLG negotiates the details of Hong Kong's transition to Chinese rule.
Chinese representative Chen Zuo'er told reporters that the territory's future leader Tung Chee-hwa has been kept informed of progress on the talks and had given his support.

While a deal on the 1997/98 (April-March) budget has been struck, a host of other matters remains unresolved ahead of the handover at midnight on June 30, including residency rights and details surrounding the stationing of the Chinese garrison here.
Britain urged China to speed up the work.
"There are some clear priorities and there is a lot of work still to be done," Hugh Davies, leader of the JLG British team, told reporters.
"The priority that I would put at the top of the list is to reach final agreement on the substance of the right of abode issue ... which has been dragging for too long," Davies said.
Other outstanding issues are the size and arrival of an advance party of China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) which will replace the British military garrison.
A number of air service agreements with foreign countries still need to be hammered out, Davies added.
